### **High Levels of Omega Fatty Acids**  
- Krill oil contains more omega-3 fatty acids, EPA, and DHA than most seafood. These fats are essential for optimal brain function and development, reducing inflammation, and maintaining healthy skin and hair because the human body can’t synthesize them.
- Additionally, these fatty acids also contribute to improved joint flexibility over time. They’ve been shown to improve heart health by reducing bad cholesterol levels in your blood and overall cardiovascular disease risk in people with metabolic conditions like diabetes. They also benefit pregnant mothers as they may improve fetal cognitive development.
- One unique feature of krill oil is that your body easily absorbs its omega-3-rich phospholipids. Phospholipid-bound omega-3s tend to reach cell membranes more effectively than triglyceride-based fatty acids in regular fish oils – this contributes to many of the observed health benefits derived from supplementing with omega-3s.  
It’s essential to note that using krill oil supplements should only be considered as a medical treatment for existing conditions with proper consultation with a medical professional beforehand.
## **Health Benefits of Krill Oil**  
- Krill oil has long been touted as one of the most widely-used products for promoting brain and heart health due to the concentration of omega-3 fatty acids Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) and Eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA). EPA has been shown to improve blood lipids such as triglycerides while reducing elevated high-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels.
- Both EPA and DHA work together to regulate inflammation, benefiting joint health by supporting flexibility while aiding cardiac function.
- Krill harvesting has raised concerns with conservationists about the commercial fishing industry’s practices. There are concerns over potential ecological impacts as food sources are threatened for animals dependent on krill.
